summary: This bill amends the National Security Act of 1947 to make unauthorized access to intelligence community property marked as closed or restricted a federal crime, punishable by up to 180 days in prison for a first offense, 3 years for a second, and 10 years for any later offense.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates new criminal penalties for unauthorized access to intelligence community property but contains no provisions related to government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures. Any minor administrative or enforcement costs are incidental and not addressed in the text.
No provisions in the bill address tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any tax-related matters.
The bill has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, public health programs, or medical regulations.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the legislation.
The bill does not mention immigration, border security, visas, or related enforcement mechanisms.
No content in the bill pertains to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.

While the intelligence community overlaps with national security functions, the bill addresses only property access rules and penalties; it contains no language on defense budgets, military funding levels, or procurement.
The legislation has zero engagement with environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation measures.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, entitlements, food assistance, or social services.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, curriculum, or school choice policies.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement appear.

The bill adds a new federal criminal offense with escalating penalties (fines and imprisonment up to 10 years for repeat offenses) for unauthorized access to marked intelligence community property. This directly expands criminal liability and enforcement in a narrow domain, aligning modestly with tougher sentencing rather than reform or rehabilitation.
No provisions concern tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or globalization.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content relates to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation contains no references to foreign assistance, international aid, or related funding.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral processes.
The bill focuses exclusively on physical property access restrictions and does not regulate data privacy, technology oversight, or surveillance authorities.
No language pertains to worker protections, union rights, or employment regulations.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions, civil rights protections, or anti-discrimination rules.
